nodes.description: External function delegatecall_selfdestruct(address _target) that performs an arbitrary delegatecall to a caller-supplied address and returns the success flag; no access control on the caller.
Caller-controlled address parameter _target used as the delegatecall destination, allowing arbitrary external code to be executed in this contract's storage context.
Named return variable _ans that receives the boolean result of the delegatecall (including the 0.4.x behavior of returning false only on revert/failure).

Low-level _target.delegatecall(...) executed with this contract's storage and address, unbounded to any whitelisted callee; enables execution of arbitrary code (e.g. selfdestruct) and full control of the contract.

edges.reason: The externally supplied parameter _target flows directly into the delegatecall destination, letting any caller choose the code executed in this contract's context.
The function body unconditionally reaches the _target.delegatecall(...) statement; no guard, owner check or whitelist gates the call.
The boolean success flag produced by the delegatecall is assigned to the local return variable _ans.
The local variable _ans is the named return value that the function returns to the caller.

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter _target has no independent semantic role: it is consumed solely as the delegatecall target, so it collapses into the unsafe delegatecall operation node.
The local variable _ans is only the named return value of the function and carries no external effect beyond that return, so it merges into the enclosing function node.
